# Report on `region.fasta` (`>locus_007`)

**Sequence:** 3,000 bp, unambiguous A/C/G/T only, no lower-case/masked or N bases.

## 1. Base composition — unremarkable
A 22.7%, C 26.2%, G 28.8%, T 22.2% (GC = 55.0%). There is a mild GC-rich stretch around **1650–1725** (≈68–70% GC in 50-bp windows, peaking near 1676–1725), containing a small run of `CCAT`-type motifs (`CCATCCATCAACCC`, positions **1667–1680**) and `GCGGGCGGCC` (≈1635). Nothing else compositional stands out; CpG observed/expected ≈ 1.0 (228 observed vs ~227 expected), i.e. no CpG suppression — this does not look like vertebrate genomic DNA.

## 2. Main notable feature: an imperfect 33-bp tandem repeat array
Positions **1848–2144** consist of **nine tandem copies of a 33-bp unit**, 297 bp total:

| copy | coordinates (1-based) | identity to consensus | sequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1848–1880 | 32/33 | GCGTACATCAT**G**TCATGTCCTGAGGGCCATTGA |
| 2 | 1881–1913 | 32/33 | GCGTACATCATCTCATGTCC**A**AAGGGCCATTGA |
| 3 | 1914–1946 | 33/33 | GCGTACATCATCTCATGTCCTGAGGGCCATTGA |
| 4 | 1947–1979 | 31/33 | **C**CGTACATCATCTCAT**C**TCCTGAGGGCCATTGA |
| 5 | 1980–2012 | 32/33 | GCGTACATCATCTCAT**A**TCCTGAGGGCCATTGA |
| 6 | 2013–2045 | 31/33 | GCGTACATCAT**G**TCATGTCCTGAGGGC**A**ATTGA |
| 7 | 2046–2078 | 30/33 | GCGT**A**GATCATCTCATGTCC**T**GCGGGCCATTG**A** |
| 8 | 2079–2111 | 32/33 | GCGTACATCATCTCATGTCCTGAGGGCCAT**A**GA |
| 9 | 2112–2144 | 32/33 | GCGTACATCATCTCATGTCA**C**GAGGGCCATTGA |

- **Consensus unit (33 bp):** `GCGTACATCATCTCATGTCCTGAGGGCCATTGA`
- Copy identities range 91–100% (mean ≈ 96%, only copy 3 exact); differences are single-base substitutions, consistent with replication slippage.
- The unit is internally **CA/T-rich** (`CATCAT`, `TCAT`, `CATCTCAT` are over-represented), i.e. a minisatellite/VNTR-like low-complexity tract.
- Flanks: `…ATGCGGCGCGGAGCAAT` (left, ending 1847) and `GGTCAGCAACAAATCCTCATC…` (right, from 2145). The unit appears nowhere else in the sequence, in either orientation, so this is a single tandem array rather than a dispersed repeat family.

## 3. No convincing coding sequence
- Longest ORF on the **reverse strand spans 1610–2122** (513 bp, 171 codons). Its 5′ ATG (plus-strand 2120–2122, `CAT`) lies *inside* the repeat array, and there is no plausible Shine–Dalgarno/Kozak context; a 3-kb random sequence would be expected to carry an ORF of roughly this length, so it is not evidence of a gene.
- Next longest ORFs are 135, 111 and 96 codons (plus strand 1831–2235, 731–1063; minus strand 171–458) — all within chance expectations.
- Within the array, one frame has no stop codons (0 stops/100 codons, frame offset 1), but that is simply a consequence of the unit being 33 bp (11 codons); the other two frames behave normally (8–9 stops/100 codons).

## 4. Features explicitly *not* found
- No inverted repeats/hairpins: no perfect stem ≥ 12 bp anywhere (largest match is a single 10-bp one) → no terminator-like structures.
- No consensus promoter elements (no TATA box, no `AATAAA` polyadenylation signal), no ARS/CENP-B/telomeric satellite or transposon (Alu-like) signatures, no triplet-repeat expansions.
- Only one significant homopolymer: a single **A₈ at 2955–2962**; no other runs ≥ 7.
- Restriction-site and motif hits (EcoRI at 1364, `CCAAT` at 609/652, `GGGCGG` at 634/772, `GATAAG` at 462, `AGGAGG` at 1799, etc.) are all at the frequency expected by chance.

## Bottom line
The region has no detectable coding or regulatory signal; its one genuinely notable feature is a **~297-bp minisatellite array of nine imperfect 33-bp tandem repeats at coordinates 1848–2144** (consensus `GCGTACATCATCTCATGTCCTGAGGGCCATTGA`), embedded in an otherwise ordinary 55% GC sequence with a mildly GC-rich patch at ~1650–1725.
